+# BMW ConceptCraft AI: Core Application Implementation Plan
+
+**Delivery window:** 10–12 hours, five people, AI-assisted implementation  
+**Product:** Evidence-backed product requirements workbench for BMW Product Managers  
+**Process:** Market research and product planning, through G1 concept freeze  
+**Scope:** F70, G60/G68, G70, and explicitly labeled successor/Neue Klasse proposals  
+**Implementation:** React/Vite frontend, FastAPI backend, SQLite, structured LLM calls
+
+## 1. The Tangible Product We Are Building
+
+Build one complete decision loop:
+
+**Import actual BMW inputs → consolidate findings → draft requirements → explain and rank them → PM review → inspect history → export the approved plan.**
+
+The main screen is a requirements table. Clicking a row opens a workbench containing the requirement, its score explanation, original evidence, assumptions, and decision controls. This is the central product, not a dashboard around a hidden analysis script.
+
+### 1.1 Core User Journey
+
+1. The PM opens the app and sees the imported datasets, analysis progress, and a ranked requirements list.
+2. The PM selects a derivative, target markets, and powertrains, then runs analysis or opens a previous completed run.
+3. The app presents proposed requirements, each with its own evidence, score breakdown, evidence level, assumptions, and status.
+4. The PM opens a requirement and follows a claim to the original spreadsheet row/cell or PDF page.
+5. The PM edits a target, challenges an assumption, changes a scoring factor, approves, rejects, or defers the requirement.
+6. The app saves the change, rationale, actor, time, and before/after state; relevant scores and baseline ranks update.
+7. The PM selects approved requirements and creates an exportable G1 snapshot.
+
+### 1.2 BMW Deliverables and Their Concrete Implementation
+
+| BMW expected deliverable | What we implement | Demonstration / acceptance criterion |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| Concept and demonstrable AI-powered prototype processing heterogeneous inputs, deriving requirements, supporting prioritization, and integrating human review | Import pipeline, analysis service, requirements workbench, scoring service, and PM decision actions | Generate at least one new requirement from actual imported data and complete its review in the UI |
+| Structured sample list with ID, actionable description, linked findings/sources, score, prioritization rationale, evidence level, future assumptions/uncertainties, and decision status | The requirements table and detail response share one structured requirement model; CSV/JSON export includes all of these fields | Every displayed/exported requirement contains these fields; evidence links resolve to stored sources |
+| Defined end-to-end workflow distinguishing autonomous AI work from mandatory human review | The workflow in Section 2, analysis-run stages, and server-enforced status transitions | Explain the process from an imported record to an approved revision; AI cannot approve requirements |
+| Audit trail covering sources, consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decisions, including changes, initiator, time, and rationale | Immutable revision snapshots plus an append-only application event stream | Show the original derivation and subsequent content, evidence, score, rank, and status changes for one requirement |
+
+**Additional presentation output:** a 3–5 minute pitch built around the working decision loop and three verified example requirements.
+
+### 1.3 Delivery Targets
+
+- Import every supplied feedback row, the survey sheets, sales forecasts, and page-aware text from the option catalogs and corporate report.
+- Produce an initial sample list targeting 12–18 proposed requirements across the three vehicle lines, as the evidence permits.
+- Verify three showcase requirements thoroughly: strong support, a real trade-off, and an explicit evidence gap.
+- Support live generation for a bounded selection of signals, with real cached results available for a reliable walkthrough.
+- Have the first real end-to-end requirement working by hour 3.
+
+The essential build is the workbench, generation, ranking, review, audit, and export. Weight sensitivity and regional comparison are additions after that loop works. Separate Kanban, graph visualization, elaborate dashboards, SSO, and full engineering feasibility automation are outside this delivery window.
+
+## 2. Workflow and AI/Human Responsibilities
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    A[Import sources] --> B[Canonical comments and facts]
+    B --> C[Consolidate evidence into signals]
+    C --> D[Retrieve supporting and opposing context]
+    D --> E[AI drafts structured requirements]
+    E --> F[Validate and calculate scores]
+    F --> G[Ranked proposed requirements]
+    G --> H[Mandatory PM review]
+    H --> I[Approved revision]
+    H --> J[Edit, challenge, reject, or defer]
+    J --> H
+    I --> K[Freeze snapshot and export]
+    A -.-> L[Versioned provenance and audit events]
+    C -.-> L
+    E -.-> L
+    F -.-> L
+    H -.-> L
+    K -.-> L
+```
+
+| Activity | Implementation | Authority |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| Parse, normalize, deduplicate comments, calculate counts | Deterministic Python code | Automatic; preserve originals and report import issues |
+| Group topics, extract issue spans, retrieve relevant context | Imported annotations, explicit rules, and bounded model-assisted analysis | Automatic proposals; retain assignment method and source locations |
+| Draft requirement, metric, alternatives, and assumptions | Structured LLM output | Proposed content only |
+| Compute factor scores, evidence index, and ranking | Versioned deterministic scoring code | Automatic calculation; PM can override factors with rationale |
+| Validate a proposed target or accept an extrapolation | PM review controls | Mandatory human judgment |
+| Approve, reject, defer, reopen, or freeze | Backend decision service | PM action required |
+
+Opening a detail panel is read-only. AI never changes an approved requirement in place. A changed requirement becomes a new revision requiring review.
+
+## 3. Architecture and Repository Structure
+
+### 3.1 Runtime
+
+- **Backend:** FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn, SQLite; OpenPyXL/Pandas for workbooks; PyPDF or pdfplumber for PDFs.
+- **Frontend:** React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Lucide, TanStack Query. Add charts only where a simple table is insufficient.
+- **LLM:** one OpenAI-compatible provider through `llm_client.py`, configured with `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, and `LLM_MODEL`.
+- **Retrieval:** SQLite FTS5 for lexical retrieval in the core build. Persisted embeddings plus NumPy cosine search can be added behind the same retrieval interface.
+- **Execution:** one backend process with a background analysis worker. Persist run state in SQLite; no separate queue infrastructure.
+- **Python:** start with the existing 3.14 environment. Confirm dependency installation in hour 1; use a compatible pinned runtime if a required dependency blocks the build.
+
+SQLite stores authoritative relationships and revisions. The retrieval index only selects candidate evidence; it never becomes the source of truth for counts or citations.
+
+### 3.2 Proposed Files
+
+```text
+backend/
+  app/
+    main.py                   # FastAPI app, routes, lifespan
+    config.py                 # Environment and model configuration
+    db.py                     # Connections, schema setup, transaction helper
+    schemas.py                # Shared Pydantic request/response contracts
+    cli.py                    # Import, analysis, and audit verification commands
+    ingestion/
+      feedback.py             # Comments, raw rows, and annotations
+      studies.py              # CN/EU means and US rating distributions
+      sales.py                # Vehicle-line/region/year facts
+      documents.py            # Page-aware PDF extraction
+      mappings.py             # Countries, powertrains, categories, vehicle lines
+    services/
+      sources.py              # Source records and citation resolution
+      signals.py              # Topic buckets, issue evidence, distinct counts
+      retrieval.py            # Relevant study/option/strategy evidence
+      llm_client.py           # Structured output, bounded retry, caching
+      analysis.py             # Run orchestration and draft validation
+      scoring.py              # Factors, intervals, ECI, ranking
+      decisions.py            # Edits, transitions, revisions, challenge application
+      audit.py                # Events, hash chain, history queries
+      export.py               # Sample list and frozen G1 package
+  tests/
+frontend/
+  src/
+    api/                      # API client and types generated from OpenAPI
+    components/
+      RequirementsTable.tsx
+      RequirementWorkbench.tsx
+      SmartEditor.tsx
+      EvidencePanel.tsx
+      ScoreBreakdown.tsx
+      DecisionDialog.tsx
+      HistoryTimeline.tsx
+      AnalysisRunStatus.tsx
+    pages/
+      RequirementsPage.tsx
+      SourcesPage.tsx
+      ReviewPackagePage.tsx
+    App.tsx
+contracts/                    # Agreed example payloads; synthetic fixtures labeled
+var/                          # Local DB, caches, extracted text, and exports
+```
+
+Keep raw BMW data and derived quotes, databases, caches, and exports out of public commits. Extend `.gitignore` for `var/` and credentials. Frontend development fixtures are synthetic and explicitly labeled.
+
+### 3.3 Development Commands to Provide
+
+From the repository root, after dependency installation:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python -m backend.app.cli ingest --data-dir BMW-Data
+.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
+npm run dev --prefix frontend
+```
+
+The CLI uses the same services as the API. Vite proxies `/api` to the backend, so the frontend has one relative API base path.
+
+## 4. Data Model and Real Input Handling
+
+### 4.1 Observed Data Constraints
+
+These counts come from inspecting the supplied workbooks and must be checked again by the importer:
+
+| File | Raw rows | Distinct feedback IDs |
+| :--- | ---: | ---: |
+| `F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | 4,076 | 2,128 |
+| `G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | 5,005 | 4,000 |
+| `G70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | 4,690 | 4,000 |
+| **Total** | **13,771** | **10,128** |
+
+Repeated IDs have the same text and different category/type annotations. Preserve the rows and annotations; count a canonical comment once per signal. These are distinct comments, not proven distinct customers.
+
+Other important constraints:
+
+- No China free-text feedback is supplied. China evidence comes from studies and other applicable sources.
+- About 90.2% of distinct G60 comments and 94.8% of distinct G70 comments are US comments.
+- F70 is ICE-only in this feedback dataset, and its supplied US/CN forecast volumes are zero.
+- China 5 Series studies refer to G68; EU studies refer to G60. Regional differences may also reflect derivative differences.
+- `BEVE` is a source value; normalize it to `BEV` while retaining the original.
+- Feedback lacks dates. The core app shows coverage and sentiment/type distribution, not sentiment velocity.
+
+### 4.2 Storage Contract
+
+Use relational identifiers and JSON payloads for complex versioned structures to keep implementation short. All source-derived entities point to immutable source versions.
+
+| Table | Essential fields / purpose |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `source_files` | `id`, filename, SHA-256, kind, imported timestamp, import summary; same file hash is idempotent |
+| `source_records` | `id`, `source_file_id`, locator JSON, raw payload JSON, optional `feedback_id`; one record per spreadsheet row or extracted fact location |
+| `feedback_comments` | `id`, source version, original ID, source label, derivative, country, region, normalized/original powertrain, original text |
+| `feedback_annotations` | `id`, `feedback_id`, `source_record_id`, original feedback type and VFC level 2/3 labels |
+| `facts` | `id`, kind (`survey`, `sales`, `option`), derivative/line, region, powertrain if known, year, metric, value/distribution, unit/scale metadata, source record references |
+| `document_chunks` | `id`, source file, 1-based PDF page, optional printed page label, chunk text, derivative/market metadata; FTS5 index |
+| `signals` | Composite key `(id, revision)`, title, category, source scope, consolidation method/configuration, summary JSON, analysis run ID |
+| `signal_links` | Signal ID/revision, feedback ID, original-text span, polarity, assignment method, annotation/source references; distinct comment counting despite multiple spans |
+| `requirements` | `id`, current revision, current status, approved revision or null; compact current-state index |
+| `requirement_revisions` | Composite key `(req_id, revision)`, full requirement payload, score breakdown, evidence links, source/signal versions, actor, timestamp, rationale |
+| `analysis_runs` | `id`, requested scope, source/config versions, stage, state, progress counts, failures, timings, model/prompt version, result IDs |
+| `scoring_configs` | `id`, formula version, factor weights, thresholds, normalization reference, forecast year; immutable once used |
+| `ranking_snapshots` | `id`, scoring config, requirement revisions, baseline ID-to-rank/score mapping, timestamp, triggering event |
+| `audit_events` | `id`, entity type/ID/revision, UTC time, actor kind/ID, action, before/after JSON, rationale, run/config references, previous/current hash |
+| `freeze_snapshots` | `id`, selected approved revisions, source/config versions, accepted assumptions, ranking snapshot, audit checkpoint, actor, timestamp, complete export payload |
+
+Enable SQLite foreign keys and WAL. Add indexes for feedback scope, source references, requirement status, and audit entity/time. Serialize writes through transactions; do not share one live connection across worker threads.
+
+### 4.3 Feedback Import
+
+1. Read the `Feedback_Explorer` sheet and map columns by header name, not position.
+2. Save every original row with a locator such as `{"sheet":"Feedback_Explorer","row":3}`; row numbers include the header.
+3. Canonicalize by source-file version plus supplied feedback ID. Verify that repeated IDs have consistent text and metadata; report collisions instead of silently merging inconsistent records.
+4. Save each annotation separately. A comment may contain both positive and negative annotations.
+5. Map `BEVE → BEV`, countries to the agreed commercial regions, and VFC categories to the topic taxonomy. Store mapping versions.
+6. Preserve missing labels. Any added label records its method and is stored separately from the imported annotation.
+7. Flag empty/non-informative text for analysis exclusion while retaining the source. Do not discard meaningful short text solely because it is under 12 characters.
+
+The sales workbook calls its Europe region `EU`. Document the commercial mapping for GB, Norway, and other European countries rather than treating the label as strict EU membership.
+
+### 4.4 Studies and Sales Import
+
+- **CN/EU studies:** walk category/`Mean` row pairs; identify derivative and region from the multi-row headers. Preserve each numeric cell, metric, and locator.
+- **US studies:** parse question blocks and seven rating categories into distributions. `Sample total = 1` is a 100% distribution total, not one respondent. Preserve unknown respondent counts as null.
+- Keep native scales. Never equate a CN/EU mean with a US distribution without an explicitly recorded transformation. Broad satisfaction measures cannot prove a specific interface preference.
+- Map topics to related study questions through a small reviewed mapping file. Mark the relation `direct`, `broad`, `contradictory`, or `unmapped`, with a reason.
+- **Sales:** read F70, G60_G68, and G70 sheets into line/region/year facts for 2024, 2025, and 2030. Treat G60_G68 as one sales line, not two volumes to sum.
+- Sales do not supply a powertrain split. A BEV-only proposal using whole-line volume must label it as an upper-bound proxy; no invented BEV share.
+
+### 4.5 PDF Import and Citation Retrieval
+
+- Extract each page from the three option PDFs and `BMW-Group-Report-2025-en.pdf`; record extraction failures/empty pages.
+- Chunk within pages, approximately 600–1,000 words per chunk, keeping the page boundary and exact original text.
+- For showcase requirements, verify the actual option codes/package facts and strategy passages used. Store selected equipment facts with source-page references; general-purpose table reconstruction is not required.
+- German catalog facts retain the original wording. Translations are separate derived text, and German packaging is not automatically asserted for other markets.
+- `GET /api/sources/{id}` returns a workbook-style record or document metadata; the PDF file endpoint supports opening the cited page with `#page=N`.
+
+## 5. How the Analysis Produces Requirements
+
+### 5.1 Signals: A Bounded, Implementable First Pass
+
+Start with approximately 8–12 in-scope topics: HVAC operation, infotainment/navigation, connectivity, seating/comfort, storage/space, visibility, charging UX, perceived range, driving experience, and equipment packaging. Final names come from inspected VFC categories.
+
+1. Map imported annotations into topic buckets per derivative. Keep positive, negative, and request evidence distinct.
+2. Calculate distinct-comment bucket counts and regional/powertrain coverage in SQL.
+3. Select a bounded representative set per bucket: different sources/markets/powertrains where available, positive counterexamples, and recurring friction. Record the selection method and cap; do not call it statistically representative.
+4. Ask the model to propose issue-specific signals and return exact original-text spans with feedback IDs and polarity.
+5. Validate that each span is a substring of the referenced original comment. Invalid citations are rejected, not repaired by inventing text.
+6. Persist the validated issue evidence as `signal_links`. Wider bucket members remain retrieval candidates until actually assigned to that issue.
+7. Where useful, an explicit phrase rule can scan the full bucket to add matches with the rule/version recorded. Show whether membership is model-assigned, rule-assigned, imported, or PM-confirmed.
+
+**Two counts must stay separate:** `topic_bucket_comment_count` describes the broad topic; `issue_support_comment_count` describes validated evidence for the specific issue. Never attach the entire HVAC bucket count to one narrower physical-button proposal.
+
+Initial generation processes at most four selected issue signals per vehicle line. This keeps latency, model cost, and citation review bounded while every raw source remains available for search.
+
+### 5.2 Context Retrieval
+
+For each issue signal, construct an evidence pack containing:
+
+- Supporting and opposing issue spans, with their source IDs and scope.
+- The mapped survey facts and mapping strength.
+- Applicable sales facts for the proposed scope.
+- Up to a small fixed number of relevant option/strategy chunks, filtered by derivative where appropriate.
+- Missing-market, missing-scale, packaging, and future-platform limitations.
+
+Use FTS search terms from the topic and issue title. Return source IDs, exact text, and metadata, not an untraceable generated summary. The model receives only these supplied identifiers and may cite only them.
+
+### 5.3 Structured Requirement Drafting
+
+`draft_requirement(signal, evidence_pack, planning_scope)` returns validated JSON containing:
+
+- Title and clear customer-facing requirement description.
+- The evidence-backed problem, kept separate from the suggested solution.
+- SMART fields: specific scope, measurable target/unit/test conditions, attainability rationale, relevance, and target milestone.
+- Claim-to-evidence references for the problem, rationale, strategy, and packaging statements.
+- Alternative solution suggestions when the evidence supports more than one approach.
+- Initial severity/strategic-fit/effort proposals with reasons, not a model-generated final priority number.
+- Future assumptions, limitations, contradictory evidence, and unresolved validations.
+
+Every metric, milestone, architecture assertion, and package suggestion has provenance: `SourceBacked`, `AIProposed`, or `PMEntered`, plus a review state. AI-proposed targets are displayed as proposals, not engineering facts.
+
+For example, complaints about difficult access to temperature controls can justify a usability requirement. A suggested maximum interaction count is a proposed acceptance target until reviewed. They do not establish an exact latency threshold, SOP year, existing camera architecture, or commercial uplift.
+
+### 5.4 Draft Validation and Persistence
+
+Pydantic validates the output shape. Service validation checks:
+
+1. IDs refer to supplied evidence and source versions.
+2. Quoted spans are exact; fact values match the stored facts.
+3. Supporting customer evidence exists for the problem statement, or the draft explicitly identifies a study-only basis.
+4. Markets, powertrains, source derivatives, and target derivatives are explicit.
+5. A narrow requirement does not claim the full topic count as support.
+6. Unsupported quantitative claims and future assumptions are labeled.
+7. Regulatory engineering and detailed component/BOM specifications do not replace the customer-facing requirement.
+
+Then the backend assigns a unique requirement ID, calculates scores and evidence quality, saves revision 1 with status `Proposed`, records the derivation, and refreshes the baseline ranking. Invalid drafts are retained as run failures for inspection but do not appear as valid proposed requirements.
+
+### 5.5 Run Behavior and Failure Handling
+
+Run stages: `import_check → consolidate → retrieve → draft → validate → score → completed`.
+
+Run states: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`. Return a run ID immediately, show progress, and poll while running. Execute one generation run at a time in the first build.
+
+- Cache by source/config versions, signal revision, scope, model, prompt version, and retrieved-context hash.
+- Use a bounded concurrency limit and at most one structured-output repair attempt per draft; transient provider errors receive bounded backoff.
+- Save valid requirements even if another signal fails, and report partial results.
+- On restart, mark interrupted runs as failed/interrupted rather than leaving them permanently running.
+- Missing credentials or unavailable providers produce a visible failure/configuration state. Cached results are labeled cached; no fabricated successful AI run.
+
+## 6. The Requirement Contract
+
+The backend owns this contract; frontend types are generated from OpenAPI. Complex fields live in the revision payload so history can reconstruct exactly what the PM reviewed.
+
+| Field | Required contents |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `id`, `revision` | Stable unique identifier and version number |
+| `title`, `description`, `problem_statement` | Actionable customer-facing wording and the originating need |
+| `source_scope` | Source derivatives, regions, powertrains, and relevant signal revisions |
+| `target_scope` | Target derivative/vehicle line, regions, powertrains; successor mapping if applicable |
+| `smart` | Specific, measurable target/unit/conditions/verification method, attainability, relevance, milestone; provenance and review state for targets/assertions |
+| `finding_links` | Signal versions and issue-level evidence identifiers |
+| `evidence_links` | Source/record/chunk IDs, locators, claim key, relation (`supports`, `contradicts`, `context`), and validation state |
+| `score` | Calculated and effective priority, factor values/contributions, input references, override if any, configuration ID, provisional flag, range |
+| `prioritization_rationale` | Deterministic explanation of main score drivers plus grounded trade-off notes |
+| `evidence` | ECI value/level, component values, distinct supporting comments, coverage, and explicit gaps |
+| `assumptions`, `uncertainties` | Future-facing statements, missing evidence, owner/review state, and any PM acceptance rationale |
+| `status`, `approved_revision` | Decision state and the exact revision approved, if any |
+| `run_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` | Derivation/run references and timestamps |
+
+Source scope and target scope are separate. A G60 complaint can inform a successor proposal, but the app must label the carryover assumption rather than claiming successor architecture compatibility.
+
+## 7. Deterministic Scoring and Evidence Quality
+
+### 7.1 Priority Formula
+
+Normalize all four factors to `[0,1]`:
+
+```text
+Priority = 100 × (0.40 × CustomerValue
+                + 0.25 × AddressableReach
+                + 0.20 × StrategicFit
+                + 0.15 × EaseOfImplementation)
+```
+
+Weights are an explicit PM policy, not learned truth. Store them with the formula version. The core build uses one immutable baseline config; what-if previews do not silently change the baseline or approvals.
+
+**Customer value:**
+
+- Severity levels 1–4: cosmetic/minor friction; repeated usability friction; core experience unreliable or difficult; core experience unavailable/major recurring blocker.
+- `severity = level / 4`, with source-linked rationale and an explicit provisional marker for AI estimation.
+- For each applicable observed region, `p_r = distinct issue-support comments / distinct available comments in the matching source-derivative/powertrain cohort`.
+- `mention = sqrt(mean(p_r))` across observed target regions. Show per-region denominators; missing regions are gaps, not zero demand.
+- `CustomerValue = 0.60 × severity + 0.40 × mention`.
+- This is a within-dataset mention signal, not population prevalence. Study-only drafts have a provisional customer factor until PM judgment; survey measures appear as corroboration rather than being silently mixed across scales.
+
+**Addressable reach:**
+
+- Sum applicable 2030 sales facts over unique `(vehicle_line, region)` keys.
+- `AddressableReach = target_volume / reference_volume`.
+- `reference_volume` is the fixed total of the supplied 2030 forecast across all supported lines/regions, saved in the config; it does not depend on the currently visible requirements.
+- Mark future-line carryover forecasts and whole-line powertrain proxies as assumptions. Zero-volume F70 US/CN scope is surfaced explicitly.
+
+**Strategic fit:** levels 0–4, mapped to `level / 4`: explicit conflict, limited alignment, partial alignment, strong alignment, direct strategic contribution. Require a cited strategy passage and a rationale. Missing assessment is unknown, not verified neutral alignment.
+
+**Ease of implementation:** complexity levels 1–5: software/UI change; calibration/configuration; existing hardware/packaging change; new subsystem integration; major architecture change. `Ease = (5 - complexity) / 4`. This is a rough proposal, not an engineering feasibility certificate.
+
+Unknown factors use a clearly marked provisional midpoint of `0.5`; expose a score range calculated with their lower/upper values of 0/1. Do not display an unknown factor as a sourced fact. Targets with no valid comparable volume require a provisional reach factor.
+
+Sort by effective score descending, then requirement ID for deterministic ties. Keep calculated score and any PM score override separately. Content/evidence changes clear an old override unless the PM explicitly reaffirms it with a new rationale.
+
+### 7.2 Evidence Confidence Index
+
+Implement a transparent rubric, not a probability of correctness:
+
+```text
+ECI = 100 × (0.35 × support
+           + 0.25 × coverage
+           + 0.25 × corroboration
+           + 0.15 × assignment_validation)
+```
+
+- `support = min(1, log(1 + distinct_support_comments) / log(51))`; study-only cases report unknown respondent support rather than manufacturing comment counts.
+- `coverage` is the fraction of target regions with applicable customer feedback or a relevant mapped study. Show which type each region has.
+- `corroboration`: 0 for no independent relevant support, 0.5 for broad same-topic support, 1 for directly relevant corroboration; contradictory evidence is separately flagged.
+- `assignment_validation`: mean membership-review value, 0.5 for traceable but unreviewed imported/rule/model assignment and 1 for PM-confirmed assignment. Untraceable assignments are rejected.
+- Evidence levels: `Low < 40`, `Moderate 40–69`, `High ≥ 70`; thresholds and components are versioned policy choices.
+
+Always show low-support warnings, unknown respondent counts, source concentration, future assumptions, and regional gaps alongside the index. High ECI does not establish an AI-proposed target or architecture claim. Priority and ECI are independent; do not hide promising low-evidence requirements by multiplying the scores.
+
+### 7.3 Regional Differences and Optional Sensitivity
+
+- Different satisfaction means produce a `satisfaction_difference` observation, not an inferred preference for touch versus physical controls.
+- Explicit opposing preferences produce a `supported_conflict` with both evidence sets.
+- Missing regional evidence produces a `coverage_gap`.
+- G60 versus G68 comparisons include a derivative-confounding note.
+- Where a real conflict exists, draft alternative regional scopes for PM review.
+- A preview endpoint accepts alternate factor weights and returns old/new scores, rank movement, and drivers. Preview results are labeled and excluded from baseline audit/approval mutations.
+
+## 8. PM Review, Revisions, and Audit
+
+### 8.1 Status Model
+
+Persistent statuses: `Proposed`, `UnderReview`, `Approved`, `Rejected`, `Deferred`.
+
+```text
+Proposed → UnderReview                 explicit Start review
+Proposed / UnderReview → Approved      PM approval, validation, rationale
+Proposed / UnderReview → Rejected      PM rationale
+Proposed / UnderReview → Deferred      PM rationale
+Approved / Rejected / Deferred → UnderReview   explicit reopen/edit
+```
+
+Challenge is an action with a separate run/result, not a new decision status. G1 inclusion is a freeze-snapshot selection, not another ambiguous status.
+
+### 8.2 Editing and Decisions
+
+Every mutation includes `expected_revision`, actor identity, and rationale. The server reads the current revision, validates the action, builds a complete new revision, recomputes affected factors, records the event, and refreshes baseline ranking within one transaction.
+
+Return HTTP 409 on stale revisions and let the UI reload/compare. Return 422 for missing rationale or invalid transitions. Use server-confirmed updates for approval/edit actions; do not show an optimistic approval before it succeeds.
+
+Approval requires:
+
+- Complete, actionable SMART fields, including a measurable acceptance target and milestone.
+- At least one valid underlying finding/study source link.
+- PM review of proposed targets and milestone, and explicit acceptance or resolution of feasibility/scope assumptions.
+- The current reviewed revision; any later content, evidence, or score edit clears approval and creates an `UnderReview` revision.
+
+The prototype uses a named PM selector as actor identity. AI/system events identify the model/run or service. This supports the demonstrable workflow; enterprise authentication is a later integration.
+
+### 8.3 Challenge Action
+
+The PM enters a question such as “Does this evidence justify a global requirement?” The service retrieves the current revision and additional relevant/opposing context, then returns cited reasoning, coverage gaps, and an optional proposed diff.
+
+Record the request and response. Do not mutate the requirement until the PM selects **Apply suggestion**, confirms the diff, and supplies a rationale. Applying uses the original expected revision; a stale result must be reviewed again.
+
+### 8.4 Events and Reconstructability
+
+Record these event categories:
+
+| Event | What must be reconstructable |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `SOURCE_IMPORTED` | File version, parser/mapping version, row counts, exclusions/errors |
+| `SIGNAL_CONSOLIDATED` / `SIGNAL_REVISED` | Membership, consolidation method, counts, source scope, before/after signal snapshots |
+| `REQUIREMENT_DERIVED` | Signal/source versions, retrieved evidence, run/model/prompt references, initial content |
+| `CONTENT_CHANGED` / `EVIDENCE_CHANGED` | Previous/new revision and exact field/evidence changes |
+| `SCORE_CALCULATED` / `SCORE_OVERRIDDEN` | Inputs, formula/config, factor contributions, original/effective score, rationale |
+| `RANKING_RECALCULATED` | Previous/new baseline ID-to-rank map, scores, context, trigger; visible moves for affected requirements |
+| `STATUS_CHANGED` | Actor, previous/new status, approved revision, decision rationale |
+| `CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` / `CHALLENGE_COMPLETED` | PM question, cited response, proposed diff, application state |
+| `FREEZE_CREATED` | Approved revisions, source/config versions, accepted assumptions, actor, checkpoint |
+
+Every event has UTC time, initiator kind/ID, entity/version, and a non-empty human or generated rationale. Store model output/context references locally for AI derivations; generation is not claimed to be mathematically deterministic.
+
+Audit view combines requirement events with its linked signal/run/source events so the PM can follow the complete chain. Ranking history uses the baseline full-list context; sorting/filtering a table changes only the view and is not a governance event.
+
+For tamper evidence, hash canonical event JSON plus the previous event hash. Provide a verifier and include the checkpoint in the exported package. This is a tamper-evident local ledger relative to a trusted checkpoint, not a claim that a database administrator cannot rewrite history.
+

+## 10. Export Behavior
+
+### 10.1 Structured Sample List
+
+CSV/JSON export includes ID, revision, description/SMART fields, linked finding/source identifiers and locators, score and factor breakdown, prioritization rationale, evidence index/level, future assumptions, uncertainties, and decision status.
+
+JSON retains nested structures. CSV flattens the main fields and serializes evidence/assumption arrays predictably; it must not silently omit them.
+
+### 10.2 Frozen G1 Package
+
+`POST /api/freezes` validates that each supplied revision is current and approved and that the baseline ranking context has not changed. It captures full requirement payloads, score/configuration, source/signal versions, decisions, accepted assumptions, and an audit checkpoint in one transaction.
+
+Generate Markdown and JSON from that stored snapshot. Later edits to a requirement do not change an existing package. PDF can be added using browser print after the core exports work.
+
+The Markdown package contains an executive summary, prioritized approved list, SMART descriptions, source references, scoring rationale, confidence/coverage, open validations, and decision history. Include a machine-readable manifest and checkpoint for verification.

+## 12. Verification and Demonstration
+
+### 12.1 Meaningful Checks
+
+- **Import correctness:** expected raw/distinct counts; repeated-ID annotations survive; mixed positive/negative comments remain multi-topic; rerunning the same import is idempotent.
+- **Provenance:** sampled comments, survey cells, volume facts, and cited PDF passages match the actual source. All generated citation IDs resolve.
+- **Signal counts:** duplicate annotations and multiple spans do not inflate distinct-comment support; broad bucket counts cannot become narrow-issue counts.
+- **Scoring:** factors stay bounded, weights sum to one, missing inputs remain provisional, same inputs/config reproduce scores, volume keys are not double-counted, complexity importance affects scores as specified.
+- **Workflow:** AI cannot approve; a blank rationale fails; stale revision fails; editing an approved requirement invalidates approval; failed writes cannot leave an unlogged state change.
+- **History:** derivation, consolidation, evidence edits, factor/score changes, resulting rank moves, and PM decisions are reconstructable with actors/times/reasons.
+- **Freeze:** unapproved/stale revisions cannot be frozen; changing the live requirement does not change an existing package; all required sample-list fields survive export.
+- **Recovery:** cached/live runs are distinguished, partial failures display, saved decisions/history survive restart, and changed audit events fail verification against the trusted checkpoint.
+
+Use focused backend/integration tests for these invariants and one browser walkthrough. Avoid spending the window on exhaustive UI unit tests.
+
+### 12.2 Three Showcase Cases
+
+Select cases after inspecting actual evidence; do not hard-code assumed complaint counts or regional preferences.
+
+1. **Strong support:** recurring issue with valid quotes and relevant corroboration.
+2. **Trade-off:** a genuine conflict or two plausible solutions with traceable evidence and effort differences.
+3. **Evidence gap:** a valuable successor/regional proposal whose applicability or target needs validation.
+
+The demonstration follows one case through drafting, score explanation, original evidence, PM modification, approval, history, and export. The other two show why uncertainty and trade-offs are useful decision outputs.
+
+### 12.3 Definition of Done
+
+- [ ] Prototype imports the supplied heterogeneous data and exposes actual import/coverage state.
+- [ ] A new proposed requirement can be generated from real findings in the app.
+- [ ] The structured sample list contains every BMW-required field and exports successfully.
+- [ ] Every requirement has traceable findings/sources and a reproducible score rationale.
+- [ ] Proposed targets, future assumptions, evidence gaps, and conflicts are visible.
+- [ ] PM edit, challenge, approve, reject, and defer work with revisions and rationale.
+- [ ] Audit history traces sources → consolidation → requirement → score/rank → human decision.
+- [ ] Relevant content, evidence, score, priority, and status changes record initiator, timestamp, and rationale.
+- [ ] Approved revisions can be frozen/exported without later edits altering the snapshot.
+- [ ] Three verified examples and a rehearsed 3–5 minute pitch demonstrate the complete core loop.
+
+**Measure the prototype's actual contribution:** time to first cited draft, time to review a requirement, and traceability coverage. Present acceleration of these activities rather than claiming the entire two-year development process has been eliminated.

235: 
236: ### 5.1 Signals: A Bounded, Implementable First Pass

240: 1. Map imported annotations into topic buckets per derivative. Keep positive, negative, and request evidence distinct.
241: 2. Calculate distinct-comment bucket counts and regional/powertrain coverage in SQL.

255:

257: - The mapped survey facts and mapping strength.
258: - Applicable sales facts for the proposed scope.

264: ### 5.3 Structured Requirement Drafting

266: `draft_requirement(signal, evidence_pack, planning_scope)` returns validated JSON containing:
267:

269: - The evidence-backed problem, kept separate from the suggested solution.
270: - SMART fields: specific scope, measurable target/unit/test conditions, attainability rationale, relevance, and target milestone.
271: - Claim-to-evidence references for the problem, rationale, strategy, and packaging statements.
272: - Alternative solution suggestions when the evidence supports more than one approach.
273: - Initial severity/strategic-fit/effort proposals with reasons, not a model-generated final priority number.
274: - Future assumptions, limitations, contradictory evidence, and unresolved validations.
275: 
276: Every metric, milestone, architecture assertion, and package suggestion has provenance: `SourceBacked`, `AIProposed`, or `PMEntered`, plus a review state. AI-proposed targets are displayed as proposals, not engineering facts.

278: For example, complaints about difficult access to temperature controls can justify a usability requirement. A suggested maximum interaction count is a proposed acceptance target until reviewed. They do not establish an exact latency threshold, SOP year, existing camera architecture, or commercial uplift.

280: ### 5.4 Draft Validation and Persistence
281: 
282: Pydantic validates the output shape. Service validation checks:
283: 
284: 1. IDs refer to supplied evidence and source versions.
285: 2. Quoted spans are exact; fact values match the stored facts.
286: 3. Supporting customer evidence exists for the problem statement, or the draft explicitly identifies a study-only basis.
287: 4. Markets, powertrains, source derivatives, and target derivatives are explicit.
288: 5. A narrow requirement does not claim the full topic count as support.
289: 6. Unsupported quantitative claims and future assumptions are labeled.
290: 7. Regulatory engineering and detailed component/BOM specifications do not replace the customer-facing requirement.
291: 
292: Then the backend assigns a unique requirement ID, calculates scores and evidence quality, saves revision 1 with status `Proposed`, records the derivation, and refreshes the baseline ranking. Invalid drafts are retained as run failures for inspection but do not appear as valid proposed requirements.

294: ### 5.5 Run Behavior and Failure Handling
295: 
296: Run stages: `import_check → consolidate → retrieve → draft → validate → score → completed`.
297: 
298: Run states: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`. Return a run ID immediately, show progress, and poll while running. Execute one generation run at a time in the first build.
299: 
300: - Cache by source/config versions, signal revision, scope, model, prompt version, and retrieved-context hash.
301: - Use a bounded concurrency limit and at most one structured-output repair attempt per draft; transient provider errors receive bounded backoff.
302: - Save valid requirements even if another signal fails, and report partial results.
303: - On restart, mark interrupted runs as failed/interrupted rather than leaving them permanently running.
304: - Missing credentials or unavailable providers produce a visible failure/configuration state. Cached results are labeled cached; no fabricated successful AI run.
305: 
306: ## 6. The Requirement Contract
307: 
308: The backend owns this contract; frontend types are generated from OpenAPI. Complex fields live in the revision payload so history can reconstruct exactly what the PM reviewed.
309: 
310: | Field | Required contents |
311: | :--- | :--- |
312: | `id`, `revision` | Stable unique identifier and version number |
313: | `title`, `description`, `problem_statement` | Actionable customer-facing wording and the originating need |
314: | `source_scope` | Source derivatives, regions, powertrains, and relevant signal revisions |
315: | `target_scope` | Target derivative/vehicle line, regions, powertrains; successor mapping if applicable |
316: | `smart` | Specific, measurable target/unit/conditions/verification method, attainability, relevance, milestone; provenance and review state for targets/assertions |
317: | `finding_links` | Signal versions and issue-level evidence identifiers |
318: | `evidence_links` | Source/record/chunk IDs, locators, claim key, relation (`supports`, `contradicts`, `context`), and validation state |
319: | `score` | Calculated and effective priority, factor values/contributions, input references, override if any, configuration ID, provisional flag, range |
320: | `prioritization_rationale` | Deterministic explanation of main score drivers plus grounded trade-off notes |
321: | `evidence` | ECI value/level, component values, distinct supporting comments, coverage, and explicit gaps |
322: | `assumptions`, `uncertainties` | Future-facing statements, missing evidence, owner/review state, and any PM acceptance rationale |
323: | `status`, `approved_revision` | Decision state and the exact revision approved, if any |
324: | `run_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` | Derivation/run references and timestamps |
325: 
326: Source scope and target scope are separate. A G60 complaint can inform a successor proposal, but the app must label the carryover assumption rather than claiming successor architecture compatibility.
327: 
328: ## 7. Deterministic Scoring and Evidence Quality
329: 
330: ### 7.1 Priority Formula
331: 
332: Normalize all four factors to `[0,1]`:
333: 
334: ```text
335: Priority = 100 × (0.40 × CustomerValue
336:                 + 0.25 × AddressableReach
337:                 + 0.20 × StrategicFit
338:                 + 0.15 × EaseOfImplementation)
339: ```
340: 
341: Weights are an explicit PM policy, not learned truth. Store them with the formula version. The core build uses one immutable baseline config; what-if previews do not silently change the baseline or approvals.
342: 
343: **Customer value:**
344: 
345: - Severity levels 1–4: cosmetic/minor friction; repeated usability friction; core experience unreliable or difficult; core experience unavailable/major recurring blocker.
346: - `severity = level / 4`, with source-linked rationale and an explicit provisional marker for AI estimation.
347: - For each applicable observed region, `p_r = distinct issue-support comments / distinct available comments in the matching source-derivative/powertrain cohort`.
348: - `mention = sqrt(mean(p_r))` across observed target regions. Show per-region denominators; missing regions are gaps, not zero demand.
349: - `CustomerValue = 0.60 × severity + 0.40 × mention`.
350: - This is a within-dataset mention signal, not population prevalence. Study-only drafts have a provisional customer factor until PM judgment; survey measures appear as corroboration rather than being silently mixed across scales.
351: 
352: **Addressable reach:**
353: 
354: - Sum applicable 2030 sales facts over unique `(vehicle_line, region)` keys.
355: - `AddressableReach = target_volume / reference_volume`.
356: - `reference_volume` is the fixed total of the supplied 2030 forecast across all supported lines/regions, saved in the config; it does not depend on the currently visible requirements.
357: - Mark future-line carryover forecasts and whole-line powertrain proxies as assumptions. Zero-volume F70 US/CN scope is surfaced explicitly.
358: 
359: **Strategic fit:** levels 0–4, mapped to `level / 4`: explicit conflict, limited alignment, partial alignment, strong alignment, direct strategic contribution. Require a cited strategy passage and a rationale. Missing assessment is unknown, not verified neutral alignment.
360: 
361: **Ease of implementation:** complexity levels 1–5: software/UI change; calibration/configuration; existing hardware/packaging change; new subsystem integration; major architecture change. `Ease = (5 - complexity) / 4`. This is a rough proposal, not an engineering feasibility certificate.
362: 
363: Unknown factors use a clearly marked provisional midpoint of `0.5`; expose a score range calculated with their lower/upper values of 0/1. Do not display an unknown factor as a sourced fact. Targets with no valid comparable volume require a provisional reach factor.
364: 
365: Sort by effective score descending, then requirement ID for deterministic ties. Keep calculated score and any PM score override separately. Content/evidence changes clear an old override unless the PM explicitly reaffirms it with a new rationale.
366: 
367: ### 7.2 Evidence Confidence Index
368: 
369: Implement a transparent rubric, not a probability of correctness:
370: 
371: ```text
372: ECI = 100 × (0.35 × support
373:            + 0.25 × coverage
374:            + 0.25 × corroboration
375:            + 0.15 × assignment_validation)
376: ```
377: 
378: - `support = min(1, log(1 + distinct_support_comments) / log(51))`; study-only cases report unknown respondent support rather than manufacturing comment counts.
379: - `coverage` is the fraction of target regions with applicable customer feedback or a relevant mapped study. Show which type each region has.
380: - `corroboration`: 0 for no independent relevant support, 0.5 for broad same-topic support, 1 for directly relevant corroboration; contradictory evidence is separately flagged.
381: - `assignment_validation`: mean membership-review value, 0.5 for traceable but unreviewed imported/rule/model assignment and 1 for PM-confirmed assignment. Untraceable assignments are rejected.
382: - Evidence levels: `Low < 40`, `Moderate 40–69`, `High ≥ 70`; thresholds and components are versioned policy choices.
383: 
384: Always show low-support warnings, unknown respondent counts, source concentration, future assumptions, and regional gaps alongside the index. High ECI does not establish an AI-proposed target or architecture claim. Priority and ECI are independent; do not hide promising low-evidence requirements by multiplying the scores.
385: 
386: ### 7.3 Regional Differences and Optional Sensitivity
387: 
388: - Different satisfaction means produce a `satisfaction_difference` observation, not an inferred preference for touch versus physical controls.
389: - Explicit opposing preferences produce a `supported_conflict` with both evidence sets.
390: - Missing regional evidence produces a `coverage_gap`.
391: - G60 versus G68 comparisons include a derivative-confounding note.
392: - Where a real conflict exists, draft alternative regional scopes for PM review.
393: - A preview endpoint accepts alternate factor weights and returns old/new scores, rank movement, and drivers. Preview results are labeled and excluded from baseline audit/approval mutations.
394: 
395: ## 8. PM Review, Revisions, and Audit
396: 
397: ### 8.1 Status Model
398: 
399: Persistent statuses: `Proposed`, `UnderReview`, `Approved`, `Rejected`, `Deferred`.
400: 
401: ```text
402: Proposed → UnderReview                 explicit Start review
403: Proposed / UnderReview → Approved      PM approval, validation, rationale
404: Proposed / UnderReview → Rejected      PM rationale
405: Proposed / UnderReview → Deferred      PM rationale
406: Approved / Rejected / Deferred → UnderReview   explicit reopen/edit
407: ```
408: 
409: Challenge is an action with a separate run/result, not a new decision status. G1 inclusion is a freeze-snapshot selection, not another ambiguous status.
410: 
411: ### 8.2 Editing and Decisions
412: 
413: Every mutation includes `expected_revision`, actor identity, and rationale. The server reads the current revision, validates the action, builds a complete new revision, recomputes affected factors, records the event, and refreshes baseline ranking within one transaction.
414: 
415: Return HTTP 409 on stale revisions and let the UI reload/compare. Return 422 for missing rationale or invalid transitions. Use server-confirmed updates for approval/edit actions; do not show an optimistic approval before it succeeds.
416: 
417: Approval requires:
418: 
419: - Complete, actionable SMART fields, including a measurable acceptance target and milestone.
420: - At least one valid underlying finding/study source link.
421: - PM review of proposed targets and milestone, and explicit acceptance or resolution of feasibility/scope assumptions.
422: - The current reviewed revision; any later content, evidence, or score edit clears approval and creates an `UnderReview` revision.
423: 
424: The prototype uses a named PM selector as actor identity. AI/system events identify the model/run or service. This supports the demonstrable workflow; enterprise authentication is a later integration.
425: 
426: ### 8.3 Challenge Action
427: 
428: The PM enters a question such as “Does this evidence justify a global requirement?” The service retrieves the current revision and additional relevant/opposing context, then returns cited reasoning, coverage gaps, and an optional proposed diff.
429: 
430: Record the request and response. Do not mutate the requirement until the PM selects **Apply suggestion**, confirms the diff, and supplies a rationale. Applying uses the original expected revision; a stale result must be reviewed again.
431: 
432: ### 8.4 Events and Reconstructability
433: 
434: Record these event categories:
435: 
436: | Event | What must be reconstructable |
437: | :--- | :--- |
438: | `SOURCE_IMPORTED` | File version, parser/mapping version, row counts, exclusions/errors |
439: | `SIGNAL_CONSOLIDATED` / `SIGNAL_REVISED` | Membership, consolidation method, counts, source scope, before/after signal snapshots |
440: | `REQUIREMENT_DERIVED` | Signal/source versions, retrieved evidence, run/model/prompt references, initial content |
441: | `CONTENT_CHANGED` / `EVIDENCE_CHANGED` | Previous/new revision and exact field/evidence changes |
442: | `SCORE_CALCULATED` / `SCORE_OVERRIDDEN` | Inputs, formula/config, factor contributions, original/effective score, rationale |
443: | `RANKING_RECALCULATED` | Previous/new baseline ID-to-rank map, scores, context, trigger; visible moves for affected requirements |
444: | `STATUS_CHANGED` | Actor, previous/new status, approved revision, decision rationale |
445: | `CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` / `CHALLENGE_COMPLETED` | PM question, cited response, proposed diff, application state |
446: | `FREEZE_CREATED` | Approved revisions, source/config versions, accepted assumptions, actor, checkpoint |
447: 
448: Every event has UTC time, initiator kind/ID, entity/version, and a non-empty human or generated rationale. Store model output/context references locally for AI derivations; generation is not claimed to be mathematically deterministic.
449: 
450: Audit view combines requirement events with its linked signal/run/source events so the PM can follow the complete chain. Ranking history uses the baseline full-list context; sorting/filtering a table changes only the view and is not a governance event.
451: 
452: For tamper evidence, hash canonical event JSON plus the previous event hash. Provide a verifier and include the checkpoint in the exported package. This is a tamper-evident local ledger relative to a trusted checkpoint, not a claim that a database administrator cannot rewrite history.
453: 
454: ## 9. API and Frontend Contracts
455: 
456: ### 9.1 API Endpoints
457: 
458: | Endpoint | Purpose / payload |
459: | :--- | :--- |
460: | `GET /api/sources` | Import state, file hashes, row/comment counts, parsing issues |
461: | `GET /api/sources/{id}` | Source metadata and workbook record/fact location |
462: | `GET /api/sources/{id}/file` | Allowlisted imported PDF download/view |
463: | `POST /api/import-runs` | Import the configured local BMW dataset; returns an analysis-compatible run ID |
464: | `POST /api/analysis-runs` | Requested scope, selected signals/topics, max drafts, refresh/cache option; returns run ID |
465: | `GET /api/analysis-runs/{id}` | State/stage, progress, failures, model/cache mode, resulting requirement IDs |
466: | `GET /api/signals` | Consolidated findings with scope, distinct counts, and evidence links |
467: | `GET /api/requirements` | Paginated/searchable table; derivative, region, powertrain, status, evidence filters |
468: | `GET /api/requirements/{id}` | Complete current revision, score, uncertainty, and decision controls |
469: | `GET /api/requirements/{id}/evidence` | Supporting/opposing/context evidence, locators, facts, regional coverage |
470: | `PATCH /api/requirements/{id}` | SMART/scope/evidence/factor edits plus expected revision, actor, rationale |
471: | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/decisions` | Start review, approve, reject, defer, or reopen; expected revision and rationale |
472: | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/challenges` | Question, expected revision, actor, rationale; returns run ID |
473: | `POST /api/requirements/{id}/challenge-applications` | Challenge run ID, expected revision, accepted diff, actor, rationale |
474: | `GET /api/requirements/{id}/history` | Revision diffs and linked consolidation/scoring/ranking/decision events |
475: | `GET /api/requirements/export?format=csv\|json` | Structured sample list, including linked evidence, score rationale, ECI, assumptions, status |
476: | `POST /api/freezes` | Selected requirement IDs/revisions, expected baseline ranking ID, actor, rationale |
477: | `GET /api/freezes/{id}` | Immutable review-package snapshot |
478: | `GET /api/freezes/{id}/export?format=markdown\|json` | G1 package from the stored snapshot |
479: | `POST /api/scoring/preview` | Optional sensitivity preview; no baseline writes |
480: 
481: Register the static `/api/requirements/export` route before the `/{id}` route. Run polling uses a common response shape for import, analysis, and challenge jobs.
482: 
483: Example approval request:
484: 
485: ```json
486: {
487:   "action": "approve",
488:   "expected_revision": 3,
489:   "actor_id": "pm-demo-1",
490:   "rationale": "Reviewed linked evidence and accepted the proposed usability target for concept planning.",
491:   "accepted_assumption_ids": ["assumption-1"]
492: }
493: ```
494: 
495: The server determines the new revision, status, timestamp, score, and events. The client cannot submit a fabricated approval state or final calculated score.
496: 
497: ### 9.2 Main Screen
498: 
499: Header: dataset/run state, **Run analysis**, **Export sample list**, **Create review package**.
500: 
501: Filters: source/target derivative, region, powertrain, status, evidence level, text search.
502: 
503: Table columns: rank, ID/title, target scope, effective priority, evidence level, uncertainty/conflict badges, status. Row selection opens the workbench. Empty, failed, partial, and cached states are explicit.
504: 
505: ### 9.3 Workbench
506: 
507: Use tabs or sections within one large drawer/panel:
508: 
509: - **Requirement:** problem, description, editable SMART fields, target provenance, alternatives, assumptions.
510: - **Why this priority:** four factor values, weighted contributions, input references, provisional range, override controls, generated score rationale.
511: - **Evidence:** verbatim spans, source/type, worksheet/cell/page link, support/opposition label, bucket-versus-issue counts, regional coverage and survey context.
512: - **History:** chronological events and revision diff, including score/rank/status moves.
513: 
514: Persistent actions: **Start review**, **Edit**, **Challenge**, **Approve**, **Reject**, **Defer**. A decision dialog requires rationale and shows outstanding targets/assumptions. Invalid actions are disabled and server-enforced.
515: 
516: After a confirmed mutation, invalidate requirement detail/list, history, and ranking queries. Preserve unsaved editor state if an API request fails. Show a reload/compare prompt for HTTP 409.
517: 
518: ### 9.4 Sources and Review Package Screens
519: 
520: The sources screen shows actual imported counts, source errors, region/powertrain coverage, and source previews. The review-package screen shows selected approved revisions, unresolved-but-accepted assumptions, baseline scores, and snapshot/download controls.
521: 
522: Keep the BMW-inspired styling consistent: navy `#061a38`, blue `#1c69d4`, neutral slate, amber for uncertainty. Prioritize legible evidence and review controls over decorative charts.
523: 
524: ## 10. Export Behavior
525: 
526: ### 10.1 Structured Sample List
527: 
528: CSV/JSON export includes ID, revision, description/SMART fields, linked finding/source identifiers and locators, score and factor breakdown, prioritization rationale, evidence index/level, future assumptions, uncertainties, and decision status.
529: 
530: JSON retains nested structures. CSV flattens the main fields and serializes evidence/assumption arrays predictably; it must not silently omit them.
531: 
532: ### 10.2 Frozen G1 Package
533: 
534: `POST /api/freezes` validates that each supplied revision is current and approved and that the baseline ranking context has not changed. It captures full requirement payloads, score/configuration, source/signal versions, decisions, accepted assumptions, and an audit checkpoint in one transaction.
535: 
536: Generate Markdown and JSON from that stored snapshot. Later edits to a requirement do not change an existing package. PDF can be added using browser print after the core exports work.
537: 
538: The Markdown package contains an executive summary, prioritized approved list, SMART descriptions, source references, scoring rationale, confidence/coverage, open validations, and decision history. Include a machine-readable manifest and checkpoint for verification.
539: 
540: ## 11. Five-Person Implementation Split
541: 
542: | Owner | Primary files / responsibility | First integration handoff |
543: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
544: | **1 — Data and provenance** | `ingestion/*`, source service; imported comments/annotations, survey/sales facts, page-aware documents | Actual feedback import and source-resolving evidence payload by hour 2 |
545: | **2 — AI and consolidation** | Signal/retrieval/LLM/analysis services; structured drafting and challenge | One valid AI draft with real source IDs by hour 2.5–3 |
546: | **3 — Backend and decisions; integration lead** | Schema/contracts, scoring, revisions, audit, API, freeze/export | List/detail/edit/decision APIs and one transactional audit path by hour 2.5 |
547: | **4 — Core PM workbench** | App shell, requirements page/table, SMART editor, decision dialogs | Table → detail → edit/approve using agreed contracts by hour 3 |
548: | **5 — Evidence and verification UI** | Evidence panel, score explanation/history, sources/package UI; demo stewardship | Verbatim evidence and score breakdown for the first real requirement by hour 3 |
549: 
550: Owner 3 approves shared schema and API contract changes; Owner 1 supplies the provenance schema. Agree these in the first 45 minutes so work can proceed in parallel. Frontend works from labeled contract fixtures until the actual API arrives, then switches to real responses.
551: 
552: Each human can delegate bounded tasks to coding agents: a workbook parser, a specified UI component, the scoring module, a revision/audit service, or citation verification. Give agents file ownership, input/output contracts, and completion checks. Use separate worktrees where useful; avoid simultaneous edits to shared contracts/configuration.
553: 
554: ### 11.1 Milestones
555: 
556: | Time | Team goal | Required evidence of completion |
557: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
558: | **0–0.75h** | Freeze contracts, enums, mappings, scoring policy, provider, schema, and candidate demo topics | Shared payloads and a runnable backend/frontend skeleton |
559: | **0.75–3h** | Build the first vertical slice in parallel | Actual feedback → signal → AI draft → score → PM decision → persisted audit event, all visible in the UI |
560: | **3–6h** | Complete heterogeneous context and sample generation | Studies/sales/PDF evidence resolves; list spans the supported lines; assumptions and source gaps display |
561: | **6–8h** | Complete required workflow and exports | Content/evidence/factor edits, challenge, status transitions, rank history, sample export, frozen review package |
562: | **8–10h** | Validate and polish | Three source-checked showcase requirements, essential integration checks, complete walkthrough and pitch |
563: | **10–12h** | Buffer and optional differentiation | Sensitivity/regional comparison only if the full core loop is stable; startup/restart and rehearsal complete |
564: 
565: If the hour-3 loop is incomplete, work through that dependency before expanding the feature surface. A requirement card containing only hand-written sample text does not satisfy this milestone.
566: 
567: ## 12. Verification and Demonstration
568: 
569: ### 12.1 Meaningful Checks
570: 
571: - **Import correctness:** expected raw/distinct counts; repeated-ID annotations survive; mixed positive/negative comments remain multi-topic; rerunning the same import is idempotent.
572: - **Provenance:** sampled comments, survey cells, volume facts, and cited PDF passages match the actual source. All generated citation IDs resolve.
573: - **Signal counts:** duplicate annotations and multiple spans do not inflate distinct-comment support; broad bucket counts cannot become narrow-issue counts.
574: - **Scoring:** factors stay bounded, weights sum to one, missing inputs remain provisional, same inputs/config reproduce scores, volume keys are not double-counted, complexity importance affects scores as specified.
575: - **Workflow:** AI cannot approve; a blank rationale fails; stale revision fails; editing an approved requirement invalidates approval; failed writes cannot leave an unlogged state change.
576: - **History:** derivation, consolidation, evidence edits, factor/score changes, resulting rank moves, and PM decisions are reconstructable with actors/times/reasons.
577: - **Freeze:** unapproved/stale revisions cannot be frozen; changing the live requirement does not change an existing package; all required sample-list fields survive export.
578: - **Recovery:** cached/live runs are distinguished, partial failures display, saved decisions/history survive restart, and changed audit events fail verification against the trusted checkpoint.
579: 
580: Use focused backend/integration tests for these invariants and one browser walkthrough. Avoid spending the window on exhaustive UI unit tests.
581: 
582: ### 12.2 Three Showcase Cases
583: 
584: Select cases after inspecting actual evidence; do not hard-code assumed complaint counts or regional preferences.
585: 
586: 1. **Strong support:** recurring issue with valid quotes and relevant corroboration.
587: 2. **Trade-off:** a genuine conflict or two plausible solutions with traceable evidence and effort differences.
588: 3. **Evidence gap:** a valuable successor/regional proposal whose applicability or target needs validation.
589: 
590: The demonstration follows one case through drafting, score explanation, original evidence, PM modification, approval, history, and export. The other two show why uncertainty and trade-offs are useful decision outputs.
591: 
592: ### 12.3 Definition of Done
593: 
594: - [ ] Prototype imports the supplied heterogeneous data and exposes actual import/coverage state.
595: - [ ] A new proposed requirement can be generated from real findings in the app.
596: - [ ] The structured sample list contains every BMW-required field and exports successfully.
597: - [ ] Every requirement has traceable findings/sources and a reproducible score rationale.
598: - [ ] Proposed targets, future assumptions, evidence gaps, and conflicts are visible.
599: - [ ] PM edit, challenge, approve, reject, and defer work with revisions and rationale.
600: - [ ] Audit history traces sources → consolidation → requirement → score/rank → human decision.
601: - [ ] Relevant content, evidence, score, priority, and status changes record initiator, timestamp, and rationale.
602: - [ ] Approved revisions can be frozen/exported without later edits altering the snapshot.
603: - [ ] Three verified examples and a rehearsed 3–5 minute pitch demonstrate the complete core loop.
604: 
605: **Measure the prototype's actual contribution:** time to first cited draft, time to review a requirement, and traceability coverage. Present acceleration of these activities rather than claiming the entire two-year development process has been eliminated.

Updated [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) around a tangible core application:

**Actual BMW data → consolidated findings → AI-drafted requirements → explained ranking → PM review → audit history → export.**

The plan now includes:
- **BMW deliverable mapping:** concrete features and acceptance criteria for all four deliverables.
- **Implementation details:** repository structure, storage model, import logic, signal consolidation, retrieval, structured AI drafting, and validation.
- **Requirement contract:** every required field, including evidence links, prioritization rationale, future assumptions, uncertainty, and status.
- **App behavior:** API endpoints, requirements table, editing workbench, evidence panel, score breakdown, and decision dialogs.
- **Governance:** revision handling and audit events covering consolidation, content, evidence, scores, ranking, and human decisions.
- **Five-person delivery split:** ownership and integration milestones across 10–12 hours.

ok and how will the app work under the hood will it be a graph of agents with tools for retrieving data etc? how it the human in the loop? for a specific insight he will chat and make and agent do the modifications? what will be the final deliverables?

**The app should run as a controlled AI workflow, with retrieval tools and a contextual assistant for reviewing each requirement.** The human remains responsible for accepting changes and approving the final requirement.

The current plan describes the pipeline. I would make the agent/tool interaction explicit as follows.

## 1. What happens under the hood?

There are two useful graphs:

- **Workflow graph:** the steps that process data and produce decisions.
- **Evidence graph:** the relationships linking a requirement to findings, quotes, surveys, sales facts, and documents.

### Workflow graph

```text
PM selects vehicle, markets, and planning scope
                    ↓
           Analysis orchestrator
                    ↓
       Consolidate feedback into signals
                    ↓
        Retrieve relevant source evidence
                    ↓
        AI drafts structured requirements
                    ↓
      Validate citations and required fields
                    ↓
      Calculate scores and evidence quality
                    ↓
       Save proposed requirements + history
                    ↓
                PM review
          ↙         ↓          ↘
       Revise     Approve     Reject/defer
                    ↓
           Export approved package
```

One orchestrator controls this flow. Specialized functions handle consolidation, retrieval, drafting, validation, and scoring.

**Model calls handle interpretation and drafting. Python handles counts, scoring, database updates, and decision rules.**

### Tool-enabled AI

The AI can use a small set of read-only tools:

| Tool | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `search_feedback(query, scope)` | Matching comments and original source references |
| `get_signal_evidence(signal_id)` | Supporting/opposing spans, counts, and coverage |
| `get_survey_facts(topic, scope)` | Relevant study results and their limitations |
| `get_sales_volume(scope, year)` | Applicable forecast facts |
| `search_documents(query, scope)` | Equipment and strategy passages with page citations |
| `get_requirement_context(id, revision)` | Current requirement, assumptions, scores, and history |
| `preview_requirement_change(id, changes)` | Validation results and recalculated score without saving |

For initial generation, the retrieval sequence can be largely predefined. During a challenge, the assistant can choose additional tools based on the PM’s question.

Keep that tool loop bounded—for example, a small number of retrieval calls per response—so latency and behavior remain predictable.

### Evidence graph

The persisted relationships look like:

```text
Requirement revision
  ├── Signal revision
  │     └── Supporting / opposing feedback spans
  │           └── Original spreadsheet records
  ├── Survey facts → original cells
  ├── Sales facts → original cells
  ├── Strategy / equipment passages → PDF pages
  ├── Scoring configuration and factor inputs
  └── PM decisions and revision history
```

SQLite stores these relationships. Retrieval searches this evidence; the model does not invent the graph or calculate its authoritative counts.

---

## 2. How is the human in the loop?

There are two explicit human decisions:

### A. Accept a proposed modification

The PM reviews an AI-generated change and decides whether to apply it.

### B. Approve the requirement

The PM signs off on the current revision, including its targets and accepted assumptions.

These are separate actions. Applying a suggestion creates a reviewed draft; it does not automatically approve it.

The backend enforces this distinction. AI has no direct tool for approving requirements or silently replacing approved content.

The application also does not need to keep an agent running while the PM thinks. It saves the draft or suggestion, returns control to the UI, and resumes processing when the PM takes an action.

---

## 3. Will the PM chat about a specific insight and ask for changes?

**Yes. The chat should be attached to the selected insight or requirement, with its evidence and revision as context.**

For example:

> **PM:** “Does this evidence justify applying the requirement globally?”

The assistant retrieves the relevant evidence and might respond:

> “The linked feedback supports the issue in the US. China has a related satisfaction measure, but no direct evidence for this interface preference. I suggest limiting the initial scope and adding a China validation task.”

The response contains:

1. **Cited explanation**
2. **Evidence gaps**
3. **Proposed changes**
4. **Preview of scoring consequences**

The UI then shows a proposed diff:

| Field | Current | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Target markets | Global | US initially |
| Assumptions | General carryover assumption | Explicit China applicability uncertainty |
| Validation task | None | Validate the need with China customers |
| Priority | Current score | Recalculated preview |

The PM can **apply, edit, or discard** that proposal.

### What happens when the PM clicks Apply?

The backend:

1. Checks that the requirement revision has not changed.
2. Validates the proposed edits and evidence references.
3. Creates a new revision.
4. Recalculates affected scores and ranking.
5. Records the actor, timestamp, rationale, and before/after changes.
6. Sets the requirement to `UnderReview` if approval has been invalidated.

The PM then approves that revision separately.

### Direct editing remains available

The PM should also be able to change a target, scope, or score through ordinary form controls. Chat is useful for reasoning and proposing edits; straightforward changes should remain quick.

**The tangible interaction is: ask → inspect evidence and proposed diff → apply → approve.**

---

## 4. What exactly will the final deliverables be?

The four BMW deliverables translate into these concrete outputs:

### 1. Working application and concept

A running frontend/backend demonstrating:

- Actual heterogeneous data ingestion.
- Finding consolidation.
- AI requirement generation.
- Explainable prioritization.
- Evidence inspection.
- PM editing, challenge, approval, rejection, and deferral.
- Persisted history.

The repository contains the implementation and startup instructions.

### 2. Structured sample requirements list

Available in the UI and as **CSV/JSON**.

Each requirement includes:

- Unique ID and revision.
- Actionable description and SMART fields.
- Linked findings and sources.
- Priority score and its rationale.
- Evidence level.
- Future-facing assumptions and uncertainties.
- Decision status.

The plan targets **12–18 proposals where evidence supports them**, with three thoroughly verified showcase cases. BMW does not prescribe that count.

### 3. Explicit end-to-end workflow

A documented diagram and responsibility table showing:

- How sources become findings and requirements.
- Which activities run automatically.
- Which activities use AI.
- Where PM review is mandatory.
- How changes, approval, and export work.

The app’s run progress and review controls demonstrate this workflow.

### 4. Demonstrable audit trail

A history view and export showing:

```text
Source → consolidation → requirement draft → scoring/ranking
       → evidence/content changes → PM decision
```

It records changes to content, evidence, scores, priorities, and status, with **initiator, time, rationale, and before/after state**.

The approved review package captures exact revisions so later edits do not alter the exported decision.

A short pitch then presents these outputs through one complete working example.

---

**The core product is an evidence-backed decision workbench with an AI assistant.** The assistant investigates and proposes; the PM accepts changes and makes the decision; the backend makes that decision traceable.

-Prioritization scores must be mathematical, reproducible, and explainable:

-$$\text{Priority Score} = \frac{\left( \text{Customer Value} \times W_{\text{CV}} \right) + \left( \text{Market Volume} \times W_{\text{MV}} \right) + \left( \text{Strategic Fit} \times W_{\text{SF}} \right)}{\text{Implementation Complexity} \times W_{\text{IC}}}$$
-
-#### Factor Calculation:
-* **Customer Value ($1.0 - 10.0$)**:
-  $$\text{Customer Value} = \min\left(10, \; \left( \log_2(\text{Signal Count} + 1) \times 1.8 \right) + \text{Severity Bonus} + \text{Kano Weight}\right)$$
-  * *Severity Bonus*: Defect ($+2.0$), Difficult to Use ($+1.5$), Wants ($+1.0$).
-  * *Kano Weight*: Must-Have ($+2.5$), Performance ($+1.5$), Delighter ($+1.0$).
-* **Market Volume Factor ($1.0 - 10.0$)**:
-  * Directly computed from `sales_volumes.xlsx` addressable 2030 forecast for targeted regions.
-  * Normalizes the combined addressable volume: $V_{\text{target}} / V_{\text{max\_fleet}} \times 10.0$.
-* **Strategic Fit ($1.0 - 10.0$)**:
-  * Evaluates alignment with BMW Group strategic pillars: Neue Klasse platform readiness, circular sustainability, software-defined vehicle OTA, and premium brand perception.
-* **Implementation Complexity ($1.0 - 5.0$)**:
-  * Level 1: Minor Software OTA / UI adjustment
-  * Level 2: Existing sensor/module calibration
-  * Level 3: Interior trim / minor hardware packaging change
-  * Level 4: New subsystem / supplier integration
-  * Level 5: Major structural / platform architecture redesign

-$$\text{ECI} = \left( 0.4 \times C_{\text{volume}} \right) + \left( 0.3 \times C_{\text{source\_purity}} \right) + \left( 0.3 \times C_{\text{survey\_correlation}} \right)$$
-
-* $C_{\text{volume}}$: Scaled based on sample size ($> 50$ citations = $1.0$, $20-50$ = $0.7$, $< 20$ = $0.4$).
-* $C_{\text{source\_purity}}$: Ratio of raw ground-truth feedback vs. imputed rows ($1.0 - \text{Imputed Ratio}$).
-* $C_{\text{survey\_correlation}}$: Agreement with quantitative customer study deltas ($1.0$ if backed by survey score drop, $0.5$ if neutral, $0.2$ if unmeasured).

+### 5.1 Signals: A Bounded, Implementable First Pass
+
+Start with approximately 8–12 in-scope topics: HVAC operation, infotainment/navigation, connectivity, seating/comfort, storage/space, visibility, charging UX, perceived range, driving experience, and equipment packaging. Final names come from inspected VFC categories.
+
+1. Map imported annotations into topic buckets per derivative. Keep positive, negative, and request evidence distinct.
+2. Calculate distinct-comment bucket counts and regional/powertrain coverage in SQL.
+3. Select up to 24 comments per bucket for initial discovery: different sources/markets/powertrains where available, positive counterexamples, and recurring friction. Record the selection method and cap; do not call it statistically representative.
